speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for Health (a) what evidence is available to determine if heated tobacco products will reduce the overall risk to both the smoking and non-smoking populations; and (b) whether HSA is assessing or has assessed heated tobacco products to decide this question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Evidence from other countries suggests that heat-not-burn tobacco products are not significantly different from traditional cigarettes in terms of emissions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There would appear to be a scientific division of opinions on this question.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, I believe the British Royal College of Physicians does believe that lower risk tobacco products can be a gateway to help smokers to move away from higher risk products, tobacco-based products which have tar, although I know there are some other bodies that disagree with it.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Ministry consider two things: firstly, conducting a study to evaluate the health effects on users as well as on those in the surroundings, in terms of the passive smokers?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think that when people talk about the value of lower risk tobacco products for harm reduction, this is really debatable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have noted, HSA did some preliminary tests.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There is no significant difference in the nicotine content between the heated tobacco products and the traditional products.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We note the UK reports but despite reports from the UK, the experience of US is quite different.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The US Surgeon-General also reported that the use of e-cigarettes is closely associated with cigarette smoking among youths and young adults.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There is really no compelling reason or practical benefit in allowing such emerging products.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For heat-not-burn tobacco products, there has been no claim by anyone that these can be used for smoking cessation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If indeed these were to be used for smoking cessation, then, these products would have to comply with the rigorous requirements, undergo rigorous scientific findings to make sure that they are safe and effective, just like the nicotine-replacement therapy that is approved under the Medicine Act.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If they claim so, then, they need to show that these products are, indeed, safe and effective.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I do not think we want to do an experiment that will harm potential users.
